chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Rhythm and blues and the crisis in popular music before her retirement
summary: Back from Britain she found the singers doing rhythm and blues; she felt there was no place for her style.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Okay, so that brings us up to the time of your retirement.
Okay, we were just talking off tape about your period just before your retirement.

Yeah. What I was saying is when I came back off that tour of Great Britain I was trying like mad to get a record because I didn't have a contract with any recording company. I was just, if anything came up and somebody wanted to make a record, you know, I was there. But I had material I wanted to record and Cliff and I went down and did a demostration recording for a company that was supposed to be interested. In fact it was an agency that one of the major - booking agencies. They sent me down to make this demostration record. And I recorded two songs. I recorded "I Thought About You" and "By Myself". And I took the recording up to the agent and; 'You know, you got to do rhythm and blues.' Well, right away I knew that was the end. Well, I had a contract with this agency. We did sign a contract. So I tore up the contract and I said, forget it. So they went

into a spiel about, you know Perry Como does the rhythm and blues. I said, 'Yeah, that's all fine and good.' I said, 'But he's not noted as a rhythm and blues singer,' you know? So that didn't make me feel too good because I just didn't want to get into that rhythm and blues. And that was the end of that. As I said before, it wasn't easy for me to find an outlet. I couldn't make any records because I wasn't in. I mean, I wasn't doing what everybody was doing. So I had to just forget about it.
There was absolutely a crisis in popular music at that time.

Yeah, rhythm and blues. You see in my opinion I do not feel that - there's nothing wrong with singing occasionally whatever is currently popular. I'm not into that. It doesn't mean that I'm against it entirely. But I feel that if you try to do everything when it comes out, you're just cutting yourself up into a whole lot of little pieces, you know. I never did try to keep up with the times, even my standard repertoire of popular songs. I feel that I select them because they're songs that I not only want to do but I think they're songs that mean something. And at this

particular time a lot of the tunes that came out in the early thirties are being heard more on radio now whether anybody wants to realize it or not. I do think that we are in sort of a nostalgia stage so far as the listeners are concerned and at the same time, I still think alot of good music was written then. And there was a time when you just didn't hear it anymore.
